# Voice AI ROI: When Does Call Center Automation Pay Off?


Calculate voice AI ROI using cost per resolved request, missed calls, implementation costs, and remaining human work. Build a call center payback estimate.


[Max Gibbons](https://www.bland.ai/blog/author/max-gibbons) October 6, 2026


Updated October 7, 2026


3 min read


A fleet telematics provider was abandoning 80% of its after-hours calls. Inbound leads were also getting sent to the wrong place, with sales and support mixed together. It put Bland on website calls to qualify callers and book meetings. After-hours abandonment fell to 5%, and the company reported more than $30,000 in sales within two and a half weeks.


The value started with calls the business had been losing. A comparison based only on the price of answering an existing call would have missed it.


## **Count unanswered demand in the business case**#


In deployments like this one, teams automate existing work at a lower cost and reach customers they couldn't serve before. Those benefits need separate lines in the calculation.


For recovered sales inquiries, follow the conversation through to the sale and calculate the contribution margin on that revenue, including the telematics provider's reported $30,000. Start with abandoned calls, callbacks, and after-hours requests, then track what customers did after getting through.


More calls are the goal when they mean more customers get help. Separate new demand from repeat contacts about the same issue, then check how many of those customers got what they needed.


## **Recovered time has more than one financial outcome**#


[MyPlanAdvocate](https://www.bland.ai/customers/mpa) 's licensed agents were spending fifteen minutes per sale reading mandatory disclosures. The language had to be delivered exactly. The agents needed their licenses to advise customers on insurance plans; reading the disclosures took time away from those conversations. Bland took over the reading, and agents recovered 40 to 50 minutes each per day. The company attributes roughly one additional sale per agent per day to that time.


That is additional capacity used to generate revenue. Teams can also reduce headcount. Count recovered capacity as a cash saving when payroll or other spending falls. Include reduced overtime and avoided hires in that calculation.


If employees spend the recovered hours on other work, record what the time produces. Don't also count their unchanged salaries as money saved.


## **Payback depends on the costs that change**#


For a simple cash-payback estimate, subtract the new monthly operating costs from the old costs you will avoid. Add measured incremental contribution margin without counting the same benefit twice. Divide the one-time implementation cost by that monthly net benefit.


Suppose, purely as an illustration, that setup costs $24,000. Avoidable monthly costs fall by $10,000, while the new AI operation, including remaining human work, costs $6,000. The net benefit is $4,000 a month, and simple payback is six months. These are example inputs, not Bland pricing or a promised result.


The AI side includes implementation, usage, carrier charges, maintenance, quality review, and human transfers.[Bland's pricing](https://www.bland.ai/pricing) separates usage, platform, and transfer charges, with enterprise capacity sized to the customer. Use the proposed deployment's terms when you build the estimate.


Price completed requests, including the human work left afterward; our[IVR versus AI voice agents comparison](https://www.bland.ai/blog/ivr-vs-ai-voice-agents) follows one request through to a result you can inspect.


[Needle](https://www.bland.ai/customers/needle) reports that Bland resolves 81% of its pharmacy inventory calls without human involvement. That number is for outbound pharmacy calls. Your inbound billing queue is a different job, so use its expected completion rate and run a lower-rate case alongside it.


Include setup and the rollout period in both cases. Then return to the unanswered calls: how many additional customers got through, how many got help, and what that changed for the business.
